newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber higher in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber higher in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices improved in late trading on Wednesday after traders held on to their stocks, waiting for better bids.
"Prices have improved this afternoon after buyers declined to sell their goods because of the poor bids which ranged from 46.00 U.S. cents/lb to 46.50," said one trader.
Traders sold rubber to U.S. buyers at 46.75 overnight fob Padang for July shipment.

Traders said offer prices were quoted at 47.75 against 47.00 in the morning fob Medan for August shipment, at 47.50 against 47.00 fob Surabaya, at 47.50 against 46.00 fob Palembang and at 47.25 against 46.75 fob Padang.
Offer prices were higher at between 46.75 and 47.00 fob Pontianak and Jambi against 46.00 in the morning.
"We expect offer prices to improve again tomorrow because we've heard that Thai traders will increase offer prices," said another trader.

"We are still waiting for further details, but I don't think traders are willing to sell at cheap prices even if Thai traders change their mind and decide to stick to the current offer prices," he said.
Traders said supply of raw material had started to improve in a number of rubber centres like Medan.
